rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī considers a nominal sentence earlier in rank because a noun is simple while a verb is composite, and the simple precedes the composite.
rows.anchor: والأشبه أن الجملة الاسمية أقدم في المرتبة من الجملة الفعلية لأن الاسم بسيط والفعل مركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also offers the counterargument that a verbal sentence may be earlier because nouns are not inherently suited to being predicates of another thing.
rows.anchor: بل الفعلية أقدم ؛ لأن الاسم غير أصيل في أن يسند إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A secondary compound sentence is conditional: two complete clauses are combined by a conditional particle and a response particle, as in the sun-shining/day-existing example.
rows.anchor: وأما المركبة تركيبا ثانويا فهي الجملة الشرطية كقولك إن كانت الشمس طالعة فالنهار موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names are classified by whether their meaning prevents shared reference: proper names, generic names denoting a shared essence, and derived names such as black, meaning a thing possessing blackness.
rows.anchor: أسماء الأعلام وأسماء الأجناس والأسماء المشتقة

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: The theologians say that a proper name conveys no benefit at all.
rows.anchor: اسم العلم لا يفيد فائدة أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī agrees that a proper name conveys no attribute of its bearer but rejects that it conveys nothing, since it identifies that particular entity.
rows.anchor: حق أن العلم لا يفيد صفة في المسمى وأما ليس بحق أنه لا يفيد شيئا وكيف وهو يفيد تعريف تلك الذات المخصوصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generic names can have genus proper names: الأسد is a generic name for the lion essence, while ثعالة is given as its genus proper name.
rows.anchor: فقولنا أسد اسم جنس لهذه الحقيقة ؛ وقولنا ثعالة اسم علم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A personal proper name identifies each bearer as that individual; a genus proper name applies homonymously to each individual, whereas a generic noun denotes only their shared essence.
rows.anchor: وضعت لفظ أسامة لإفادة ذات كل واحد من أشخاص الأسد بعينها من حيث هي هي على سبيل الاشتراك اللفظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians inferred that أسامة is a genus proper name because it is diptote; its femininity was one cause, and they found no other cause besides properness.
rows.anchor: وجدوا أسامة اسما غير منصرف وقد تقرر عندهم أنه ما لم يحصل في الاسم شيئان لم يخرج عن الصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī frames the objection that if God wills the servant’s welfare, either He expects Satan to corrupt the servant, raising why He created and empowered him, or He does not, raising why refuge is needed; if God does not will welfare, refuge seems ineffective.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى إما أن يكون مريدا لصلاح حال العبد أو لا يكون فإن كان الحق هو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan is compelled to evil, this seems to conflict with the claim that God wills only good; if Satan can choose good or evil, a divine determinant is required, making seeking refuge appear futile.
rows.anchor: الشيطان إما أن يكون مجبورا على فعل الشر أو يكون قادرا على فعل الشر والخير معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Satan sinned through another satan, the explanation regresses without end; if not, the same possibility seems to apply to humans, so refuge from Satan has no utility.
rows.anchor: فإن قلنا إنه وقع فيها بوسوسة شيطان آخر لزم التسلسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God empowers Satan against people but gives Satan no satanic tempter, the unequal burden on people seems inconsistent with God’s mercy and aid to His servants.
rows.anchor: إنه تعالى سلط الشيطان على البشر ولم يسلط على الشيطان شيطانا آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that if the feared act is known to occur it is necessary, and if it is not known to occur it is impossible; either way, seeking refuge seems pointless.
rows.anchor: الفعل المستعاذ منه إن كان معلوم الوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The debate implies that seeking refuge in God has no reality unless the servant recognizes that everything is from God and through God; the Prophet prayed for refuge in God’s pleasure from His anger and in God Himself from God.
rows.anchor: هذه المناظرة تدل على أنه لا حقيقة لقوله

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī cites the Prophetic supplication seeking refuge through God’s pleasure from His wrath, His pardon from His anger, and in Him from Him, ending that praise cannot encompass Him and He is as He praised Himself.
rows.anchor: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم : أعوذ برضاك من سخطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an and reports express refuge both in God and in God’s perfect words; God’s words are His command كن, whose force is the execution of His power and will throughout possible beings without obstruction.
rows.anchor: هذا ورد في القرآن والأخبار على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instantaneous formation of spiritual beings contrasts with bodily things, which arise through motion and gradual passage from potentiality to actuality; this likeness is why the execution of divine power is called a word.
rows.anchor: الجسمانيات لا يكون حدوثها إلا على سبيل الحركة والخروج من القوة إلى الفعل يسيرا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the spiritual beings governing the bodily world with the agents described as arranging affairs.
rows.anchor: عالم الأرواح مستول على عالم الأجسام وإنما هي المدبرات لأمور هذا العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The perfect words of God are the lofty, pure spirits; human spirits seek their aid against evil, dark, impure spirits.
rows.anchor: استعاذة من الأرواح البشرية بالأرواح العالية المقدسة الطاهرة الطيبة في دفع شرور الأرواح الخبيثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge through God’s words suits someone who still attends to things besides God; full immersion in divine unity brings the servant to seek refuge only in God, as in the Prophetic prayer, I seek refuge in You from You.
rows.anchor: إنما يحسن ذكره إذا كان قد بقي في نظره التفات إلى غير الله وأما إذا تغلغل في بحر التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even the refuge-seeking rank involves attention to something besides God because it entails desire or flight; beyond it, the servant is annihilated from self and from awareness of that annihilation, absorbed in the light of the basmala.
rows.anchor: الاستعاذة لا بد وأن تكون لطلب أو لهرب وذلك اشتغال بغير الله تعالى فإذا ترقى العبد عن هذا المقام

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says in al-Umm that, although it is said refuge is sought in every rakʿa, his own position is to seek refuge only in the first rakʿa.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه في الأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A defense of Al-Shāfiʿī’s first-rakʿa-only position appeals to the default absence of obligation and says the conditional إذا in the command to seek refuge when reciting does not itself mean every time.
rows.anchor: بأن الأصل هو العدم وما لأجله أمرنا بذكر الاستعاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counterargument is that when a ruling is attached to a relevant description, that description indicates its cause, so the ruling recurs whenever its cause recurs.
rows.anchor: ترتيب الحكم على الوصف المناسب يدل على العلية فيلزم أن يتكرر الحكم بتكرر العلة

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfa require the formula seeking refuge in God from accursed Satan, matching the wording of the Qur’anic command and the apparent wording of a report from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim.
rows.anchor: فقال الشافعي : واجب أن يقول : أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم وهو قول أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: Aḥmad considers it preferable to add إنه هو السميع العليم to the standard formula, thereby combining the two cited Qur’anic wordings.
rows.anchor: أحمد : الأولى أن يقول أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of al-Rāzī’s companions prefer placing السميع العليم after بالله and before من الشيطان الرجيم, also combining the two verses.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أصحابنا الأولى أن يقول

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī reports from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that when the Prophet rose at night, he said takbīr three times and sought refuge in God, the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, from Satan.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أنه قال

rows.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Thawrī and al-Awzāʿī prefer adding إن الله هو السميع العليم after the standard refuge formula.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري والأوزاعي : الأولى أن يقول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that Gabriel first instructed Muḥammad to seek refuge in God, the All-Hearing, All-Knowing, from Satan, then instructed him to recite the basmala and the opening of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq; al-Rāzī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس أن أول ما نزل جبريل على محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge purifies the heart of what blocks absorption in God, while the basmala turns the heart toward the awe of God’s majesty.
rows.anchor: فالاستعاذة تطهر القلب عن كل ما يكون مانعا من الاستغراق في الله والتسمية توجه القلب إلى هيبة جلال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase beginning with bi-l-qalam is incomplete without an elided verb, such as كتبْتُ بالقلم; similarly, بالله in an oath implies أحلف, and على اسم الله when permitting travel implies travel in God’s name.
rows.anchor: اتفقوا على أنه لا بد فيه من إضمار فعل فإنك إذا قلت بالقلم لم يكن ذلك كلاما مفيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Omitting the implied verb is more eloquent because stating one verb would confine the phrase to that act, while omission lets the hearer infer that all needs depend on refuge in or beginning with God’s name; he compares this with saying الله أكبر without specifying a comparison.
rows.anchor: الحذف في هذا المقام أفصح والسبب فيه أنه لو وقع التصريح بذلك المضمر لاختص قوله أعوذ بالله بذلك الحكم المعين

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says this bāʾ can only govern kasra, which is why it is kasra; the simile kāf also governs kasra but is itself fatḥa because it stands in for a noun and is weak, whereas a particle exists through its effect and is strong.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه لم يكن لهذه الباء عمل إلا الكسر فكسرت لهذا السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ may be original, as in the statement that Muhammad was no unprecedented messenger, or extra, with several functions.
rows.anchor: الباء قد تكون أصلية كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ of adhesion is exemplified by أعوذ بالله and بسم الله.
rows.anchor: أحدها للإلصاق وهي كقوله { أعوذ بالله } وقوله { بسم الله }

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that the bāʾ may indicate partitive meaning.
rows.anchor: وثانيها للتبعيض عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An extra bāʾ can strengthen negation, as in ما ربك بظلام للعبيد.
rows.anchor: وثالثها لتأكيد النفي كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An extra bāʾ can make a verb transitive, as in ذهب الله بنورهم, meaning أذهب نورهم.
rows.anchor: ورابعها للتعدية كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ can mean في; the cited poetic line حل بأعدائك ما حل بي is glossed as حل في أعدائك, and oath-bāʾ is classed under adhesion.
rows.anchor: خامسها الباء بمعنى في قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī identifies Sūrat al-Fātiḥa as Meccan and says it has seven verses.
rows.anchor: سورة الفاتحة وآياتها سبع مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes the widely held report that God has 1,001 sacred names found in the Qur’an and Sunna, and says studying each name is a noble discipline requiring knowledge of the named entity, proofs for its existence, and responses to objections, collectively thousands of questions.
rows.anchor: قد اشتهر عند العلماء أن لله تعالى ألفا وواحدا من الأسماء المقدسة المطهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in the basmala expresses adhesion and attaches to an elided verb understood as I begin performing acts of obedience in God’s name; unpacking this involves true beliefs, pure deeds, proofs, and answers to objections, perhaps over ten thousand questions.
rows.anchor: باء الإلصاق وهي متعلقة بفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge in God signifies rejecting improper beliefs and deeds, while saying in God’s name signifies adopting proper beliefs and deeds; sound reason confirms this order.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى نفي ما لا ينبغي من العقائد والأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is praise for blessing, and praising a blessing presupposes knowing it; God’s blessings cannot be counted, as the cited verse says.
rows.anchor: الحمد إنما يكون حمدا على النعمة والحمد على النعمة لا يمكن إلا بعد معرفة تلك النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī illustrates the scale of the inquiry through the human body: anatomists found nearly five thousand benefits, and known examples are only a drop beside the unknown; understanding divine wisdom in human creation entails ten thousand or more questions.
rows.anchor: وجدوا قريبا من خمسة آلاف نوع من المنافع والمصالح التي دبرها الله عز وجل بحكمته في تخليق بدن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Considering divine wisdom in the throne, heavens, luminaries, elements, minerals, plants, and animals adds vast further questions; most of creation is made for human benefit, and al-hamd lillah thus encompasses roughly a million issues.
rows.anchor: علم أن هذا المجموع مشتمل على ألف ألف مسألة أو أكثر أو أقل ثم إنه تعالى نبه على أن أكثرها مخلوق لمنفعة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction rabb al-ʿālamīn is an iḍāfa, whose relation cannot be known without first knowing both correlated terms.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الشيء إلى الشيء تمتنع معرفتها إلا بعد حصول العلم بالمتضايفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿālamīn means every existent other than God; these beings comprise extended bodies, separate entities, and attributes, with bodies divided into simple and composite kinds.
rows.anchor: العالمين عبارة عن كل موجود سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says there is no proof that only the familiar kinds of bodies exist: an infinite void lies beyond this world, and God can create innumerable greater worlds containing counterparts of its cosmic features; philosophers’ arguments for one world rely on weak premises.
rows.anchor: لم يقم دليل على أنه لا جسم إلا هذه الأقسام الثلاثة وذلك لأنه ثبت بالدليل أنه حصل خارج العالم خلاء لا نهاية له
